name: Zeus
summary: King of the Olympian gods and ruler of the sky, thunder, and law. Zeus presided over Mount Olympus and was regarded as the ultimate authority among gods and mortals alike.
domain_role: Sky, thunder, law, order, kingship of the gods
origin_story: Zeus was the youngest son of the Titans Cronus and Rhea. Fearing a prophecy that one of his children would overthrow him, Cronus swallowed each of his children at birth. Rhea hid Zeus at birth, giving Cronus a stone wrapped in cloth to swallow instead. Raised in secret on the island of Crete, Zeus grew to maturity, forced his father to disgorge his swallowed siblings, and led them in the decade-long war against the Titans, known as the Titanomachy. Victorious, Zeus and his brothers divided rule of the cosmos: Zeus took the sky, Poseidon the sea, and Hades the underworld.
achievements: Led the Olympians to victory over the Titans in the Titanomachy
Established the reign of the Olympian gods and became their king
Fathered many major gods and heroes, including Athena, Apollo, Artemis, and Hercules
Served as the enforcer of oaths, hospitality, and justice among gods and mortals

signature_quote.text: In Homer's Iliad, Zeus is repeatedly described as the one whose will ultimately prevails over gods and mortals alike.
